trails.title: From probability to Active Inference
trails.summary: Start with a small update rule, then distinguish that teaching example from broader accounts of cognition and Bayesian mechanics.
trails.prerequisites: Basic fractions; familiarity with conditional probability helps with the final paper.

steps.goal: Change a prior and likelihoods. Explain why an observation changes the posterior and identify impossible evidence.
Read the interview for conceptual context. Separate discussion of the Free Energy Principle from experimental evidence.
Sample the Fundamentals onboarding discussion and note unfamiliar terms to revisit in the monograph.
Inspect the worked example's assumptions and equations; identify the extra structure beyond the binary update.

trails.title: Ants, reinforcement and collective behavior
trails.summary: Compare an abstract reinforcement process with empirical measurements and specific models of ant behavior.
trails.prerequisites: Introductory biology and probability; no programming required for the first three steps.

steps.goal: Repeat a seed, vary reinforcement, and explain which biological mechanisms the urn leaves out.
Identify the measured variables and distinguish reported associations from causal mechanisms.
Compare a specific pheromone model's assumptions and outputs with the abstract urn.
Sample the Active Inferants discussion and list the modeling choices that need their own empirical validation.
Inspect the repository's data workflow and evidence boundaries before considering a local run.

trails.title: Information commons and cognitive security
trails.summary: Move from narrative ecosystems to standards and operational agent skills, keeping conceptual and implementation claims distinct.
trails.prerequisites: Interest in information systems, governance or security; basic repository navigation for the final step.

steps.goal: Identify the framework's units of analysis and its account of conflict and trust.
Compare the role of open standards with the preceding narrative perspective.
Follow the distinctions among properties, processes and perspectives in the proposed framework.
Inspect the skill architecture and follow its associated software link; distinguish packaged guidance from demonstrated security outcomes.

trails.title: From research teams to reproducible artifacts
trails.summary: Connect research organization with an executable document pipeline and inspect the source before running it.
trails.prerequisites: Comfort reading a repository README; Python and shell experience for any later local execution.

steps.goal: Read the proposed team composition and distinguish an organizational model from measured team outcomes.
Trace configuration, computation and publication boundaries through the described architecture.
Inspect installation requirements, example inputs and validation commands before choosing a bounded reproduction.
